fullName: Eudokia Makrembolitissa, Byzantine Empress and Regent
displayNameCn: 欧多基娅·马克伦博利提萨
fullNameCn: 拜占庭女皇兼摄政欧多基娅·马克伦博利提萨
deathPlaceCn: 拜占庭帝国君士坦丁堡

events.label: Became Augusta when Constantine X took the throne
events.labelCn: 君士坦丁十世即位后成为奥古斯塔
events.note: Eudokia appeared publicly and numismatically alongside Constantine, becoming a central member of the Doukas imperial regime.

events.label: Assumed government for her minor sons
events.labelCn: 为未成年诸子摄政并掌握政府
events.note: After Constantine X's death, Eudokia governed in her own right together with the young emperors Michael and Konstantios.

events.label: Obtained release from her oath not to remarry
events.note: Because military pressure made an adult commander desirable, Eudokia secured ecclesiastical and political release from the oath imposed at Constantine X's death.

events.label: Married Romanos Diogenes and elevated him as emperor
events.labelCn: 与罗曼努斯·第欧根尼结婚并将其立为皇帝
events.note: The marriage brought an experienced military aristocrat into the imperial family while preserving the crowned rights of Eudokia's Doukas sons.

events.label: Died after long monastic retirement
events.labelCn: 长期修道院生活后去世
events.note: A death year of 1096 is widely repeated and supported by some biographical traditions, but not all prosopographical authorities treat it as fully secure.

sourceNote: Lynda Garland, Byzantine Empresses: Women and Power in Byzantium, AD 527–1204; Michael Psellos, Chronographia; Oxford Dictionary of Byzantium; Prosopography of the Byzantine World; Encyclopaedia Britannica / Encyclopedia.com biographical traditions; Wikipedia supplementary chronology.
notes:
Eudokia was Constantine X's widow, mother of Michael VII and a genuine governing figure during the 1067 minority. Her marriage to Romanos IV was a political solution to military pressure, but after Manzikert the Doukas faction removed both Romanos and Eudokia from effective authority.
